summary: I closed the last measurement-shaped gap in the VerifyLeader consequence with a source argument instead of another run. The twelve-trial receipt had left open whether a partition landing while a follower is already campaigning could put a competing leader in place before the cut-off leader stops confirming, and two gates in the follower path answer it: a node that knows a leader refuses a vote request from any other candidate before it even compares terms, so a pre-existing candidate cannot collect that vote, and the peer only clears its view and starts its own campaign when its heartbeat timer fires — a timer that the same leader keeps resetting while its own lease runs down. ValidateConfig enforces LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout per node, so in a cluster that shares settings the lease expiry is the earliest event in the sequence, and the peer then still needs a full election round; that is exactly the ordering the twelve trials measured (last confirmations at 44-49ms, competing leaders at 67-142ms) and it explains it mechanically rather than as a scheduling coincidence, with the lease check counting voters only, which is precisely why a reachable nonvoter prolongs confirmation without prolonging leadership. I recorded the mixed-timing exception honestly as the one configuration that could overlap — the relation is enforced per node, not across the cluster, and a follower with a shorter heartbeat timeout than the leader's lease would start first — noting that the captured defaults do not produce it, that this run did not construct it, and that it would need per-node configurations the cluster helper does not offer. The parent finding is unchanged in substance: the surviving defect is the unsound confirmation, while its stale-read consequence stays bounded for uniform configurations. I also recorded, as a separate excluded cause, the replication-backoff suspicion I checked earlier this session: the backoff is capped at about ten seconds and cleared by the first attempt that reaches a recovered follower, so it cannot stall replication indefinitely, though the delay itself remains as counterevidence.
